dossier.public_summary: The 0.64-day dip lands on the target but lasts far longer than expected and the star brightens and dims by ~68,000 ppm at the same 0.64-day period as the dip. The 38,000 ppm out-of-eclipse swing is as deep as the dip itself. Together this is the stellar light curve folded as a transit, not a planet transiting the star.

reasons.why: Out-of-transit swing is as large as the transit depth (1.35x) with high chi2, requiring a large ellipsoidal/thermal phase variation from a close companion, not activity on a planet host.
Dip period equals stellar rotation period exactly; star is strongly modulated at 67,589 ppm, dip is the stellar variability signal aliased as a transit.
Duration is 1.76x the central duration for the 0.389 Rsun star and fit log density ratio -1.765 with large density penalty mismatch transit shape to planet around reported star.
reasons.value: observed_h=1.486 central_h=0.8452 ratio=1.759 stellar_radius tic_radius=0.389052 duration_ratio=1.76 star_density_penalty=319.9

reasons.why: ML planet score well below 0.1 median planet, consistent with variability/binary; centroid on_target=2.784 arcsec does not outweigh phase-curve/rotation/duration evidence.
